ai.description: This slender snake reaches 60–80 cm. It is olive-brown with a distinct yellow nuchal collar and dark lateral spots. It features 17–19 midbody scale rows and a divided anal plate.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Herpetoreas sieboldii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark V-shaped mark on the nape, which is absent in other similar-looking Indian keelbacks.
ai.habitat: The Sikkim Keelback inhabits humid, forested mountain regions and stream banks within the Himalayas, typically at elevations ranging from 1,000 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Sikkim Keelback is primarily diurnal and specializes in hunting amphibians, often foraging near streams and damp forest floors to locate its prey.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Herpetoreas sieboldii* is oviparous, laying clutches of 5–12 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing by late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Herpetoreas sieboldii* occurs in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim and West Bengal, typically inhabiting elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
